skill.name: plannotator
skill.description: Visual plan and diff review for AI coding agents. It opens a browser workflow for annotations, approvals, feedback, and optional notes export.
skill.summary: Review AI coding plans, git diffs, and annotations in a browser before implementation.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: The skill provides a legitimate visual review workflow, but it has high security impact because installation and setup scripts execute or encourage remote code execution and persistently modify agent configuration. Many Markdown backtick and read-only status findings are false positives, while the installer, hidden configuration writes, temporary plan files, and shell profile editing remain confirmed risks.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash and irm-to-iex patterns with signed releases, checksums, pinned versions, and a reviewed installer file that users run after inspection.

remediation.issue: Setup scripts persistently modify AI tool hooks, prompts, and developer instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for each target file, show exact diffs, support rollback, and prefer project-scoped configuration where possible.

remediation.issue: Remote configuration writes unsanitized prompt values into shell profiles.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the port as numeric, reject newlines and shell metacharacters, and write values using safe shell quoting before appending to profile files.

remediation.issue: Plan and feedback examples use predictable /tmp file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp-created private files or directories with restrictive permissions, or pass plan content through stdin without storing it in shared temporary paths.
Recommend configuring one integration at a time and verifying status before enabling additional hooks or plugins.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Profile Injection via Remote Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The remote configuration script appends PLANNOTATOR_PORT, PLANNOTATOR_BROWSER, and PLANNOTATOR_SHARE_URL values from prompts into a shell profile without validation or shell escaping. Crafted values with quotes, newlines, or shell syntax could execute when the profile is sourced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script builds export lines from raw prompt input and appends them to the selected shell profile. There is no numeric port validation or robust shell quoting before the write.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Agent Instruction and Hook Installation
semantic_findings.description: The setup scripts install persistent hooks, prompts, slash commands, and developer instructions that change future AI agent behavior. This is core functionality, but it gives the skill durable influence over Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, and OpenCode sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited scripts explicitly define hook JSON, GEMINI.md text, Codex developer instructions, and OpenCode command files. These changes are written to user or project configuration and persist beyond the setup command.

content.user_title: Review AI Plans and Diffs Visually
content.value_statement: AI coding agents can start work before plans are clear, which makes errors costly. Plannotator adds a browser review step for plans, diffs, images, approvals, and structured feedback.
actual_capabilities: Installs the plannotator CLI and can configure integrations for multiple AI coding tools.
Adds plan review hooks for Claude Code and Gemini CLI when the setup scripts are run.
Creates Codex prompt and developer instruction files for manual plan review workflows.
Registers OpenCode plugin settings and slash commands for review and annotation.
Launches a visual git diff review workflow through the plannotator review command.
Checks local integration status for hooks, prompts, environment variables, and git changes.
limitations: The installer depends on external plannotator.ai scripts and should be verified before use.
Setup scripts modify hidden AI tool configuration files in the user home directory.
Browser review, notes export, and diff review require the plannotator CLI to be installed locally.
The skill supports review workflows, but it does not replace human technical judgment.

use_cases.title: Review an Agent Plan Before Coding
use_cases.description: Open a proposed implementation plan in a browser, annotate risky steps, and send structured feedback before code changes start.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Git Diff With Line Notes
use_cases.description: Launch a visual diff review for uncommitted work or a selected commit range, then capture focused feedback for revisions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Reviews Across Agent Tools
use_cases.description: Configure similar plan review flows for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode in one local workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Plan Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup after the CLI is installed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plannotator to review my implementation plan before coding. Open the plan review flow and wait for my approval or requested changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Git Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wants feedback on local changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open a plannotator diff review for my current git changes. Summarize the review feedback and update the code only after I approve the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an Agent Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants one supported AI tool connected.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure plannotator for my AI coding tool. Show the files that will change first, then apply the setup only after I confirm.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Review Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with plan review, implementation, and diff review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan, send it to plannotator for review, revise it from my annotations, then implement only after approval. After implementation, open a diff review and address approved feedback.

output_examples.input: A Claude Code plan proposes a database migration and needs approval before work starts.
output: The plan opens in a browser review session.
The reviewer marks the rollback step as incomplete.
The agent receives a request to revise the migration plan before coding.

output_examples.input: A branch contains uncommitted UI changes that need line-level feedback.
output_examples.output: Plannotator opens a visual diff review. The reviewer annotates specific changed lines and sends feedback for the next revision.

output_examples.input: A developer works over SSH and needs browser access to the review UI.
output_examples.output: The remote configuration workflow sets a fixed port and explains how to forward the review UI to the local browser.

best_practices: Run dry-run modes before setup so hidden configuration changes are visible.
Review plans before implementation and include acceptance criteria in requested changes.
Verify installed scripts and backups before enabling hooks across multiple AI tools.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers into a shell without independent verification.
Do not enable every integration before confirming which tools your team uses.
Do not place sensitive plans in shared temporary paths on multi-user systems.

faq.question: What does this skill help me review?
faq.answer: It helps review AI agent plans, git diffs, markdown annotations, and related implementation feedback in a browser UI.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The skill documents workflows for Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.

faq.question: Does it change my local configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. Setup scripts can write hooks, prompts, and instructions under hidden tool configuration directories.

faq.question: Can I preview changes before setup?
faq.answer: Several setup scripts include dry-run modes. Use them before writing hook or prompt files.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: The installer uses remote plannotator.ai installation scripts. Review and verify those scripts before running them.

faq.question: Can it save plans to notes apps?
faq.answer: The documented workflow supports optional Obsidian and Bear Notes export when the local CLI and UI are configured.
